sources.locator: "Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan", revision 1375661366

explanation: Both articles make the massacre the reason the city rose, and the rising is what the Spanish fled. The Fall of Tenochtitlan article, § Aztec revolt: "The massacre had the result of resolutely turning all the Aztecs against the Spanish and completely undermining Moctezuma's authority." The massacre's own article closes its lead with the consequence: "When Cortés and his men returned, the Mexica drove the Spaniards out of the city on the so-called the Sad Night (La Noche Triste), losing most of their men in battle or as prisoners who were then sacrificed." The La Noche Triste article states the intervening step — "In retaliation, the Aztecs laid siege to the Spanish compound" — which is the siege the flight broke out of. `caused` rather than `precondition-of`: the articles use causal language for it and name no other reason for the revolt. Probable: Wikipedia alone, at two revisions.
